issues.legal_issue: The statutory term “cost of construction” in calculating fair rent for a non-residential building refers to the cost of its original construction, rather than its market value or the cost of reproducing it at a later date.
material_facts: The fair-rent calculation treated construction cost and the market value of the building site as separate components of total cost.
The statute separately provided for allowances for location, architectural features, amenities, and other advantages.
The prescribed construction rates produced a fixed calculation related to the date the statute came into force, rather than a changing market value.
issues.conclusion: “Cost of construction” means the cost of the building’s original construction, with allowance for subsequent improvements as appropriate; it does not mean the building’s market value or the cost of reproducing it at a later date.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4(3)(b)(i) of the Madras Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960, construction cost is distinct from the site’s market value under section 4(3)(b)(ii). Section 4(3)(b)(iii) separately provides for allowances for location, architectural features, amenities, and other advantages. Reading construction cost as market or reproduction value would conflate the distinct statutory components and could count those advantages twice. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.rent_control_fair_rent_proceeding: The proceeding concerns fixing fair rent for a non-residential building under a rent-control scheme.
predicates.construction_cost_contrasted_with_site_m: The governing scheme treats the building’s construction cost and the site’s market value as separate components of total cost.
predicates.separate_allowances_cover_location_or_am: The governing scheme separately allows for location, amenities, architectural features, or similar advantages.

issues.definition: When a fair-rent scheme separates construction cost from site market value and separately accounts for location or amenities, the construction-cost component means original construction cost.

issues.legal_issue: A prescribed-rate rule cannot replace the statutory construction-cost measure with the cost of reproducing a building at a later date.
material_facts: The rule prescribed rates for calculating construction cost for different classes of non-residential buildings.
Those rates were used to calculate a reproduction value rather than the cost of the building’s original construction.
The fair-rent proceeding depended on applying the statutory construction-cost component.
issues.conclusion: The prescribed-rate rule went beyond the statute, and fair rent must be determined without applying that rule.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(3)(b)(i) of the Madras Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960, makes construction cost a component of total cost, while section 34 authorizes rules to carry out the Act’s purposes. Because construction cost means original construction cost, a rule prescribing rates that instead calculate reproduction value exceeds the statutory measure. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.rent_control_fair_rent_proceeding: The proceeding concerns fixing fair rent under a rent-control scheme.
predicates.prescribed_rate_rule_substitutes_reprodu: A rule prescribes rates that substitute a later reproduction-cost calculation for the original construction-cost measure.

issues.definition: In a fair-rent proceeding, a rate rule that substitutes reproduction cost for original construction cost cannot be used to calculate fair rent.
